comment: Sensitive routes referenced in JS (0.55.0). JsAnalyzer tests every link it extracts from a JS body (path only, case-insensitive; static-asset extensions skipped) against these and records one finding per (rule, route) carrying a how-to-test note. The JS Analysis tab shows whether the route was ever seen answering in captured traffic (Seen = N means 'referenced by the client but never requested yet' -- the untested surface). Keep every span bounded (ReDoS); a route is at most 300 chars.

patterns.name: Sensitive route in JS: admin
patterns.note: request it directly with a normal/low-priv session and with no session -- client-side-only gating is common

patterns.name: Sensitive route in JS: actuator/diagnostic
patterns.note: fetch it: framework diagnostic endpoints often expose env vars, heap dumps or the full API spec

patterns.name: Sensitive route in JS: internal/debug
patterns.note: non-public surface -- check it is reachable from production and what it returns or toggles

patterns.name: Sensitive route in JS: upload
patterns.note: file upload tests: extension/content-type bypass, path traversal in filename, SVG/HTML stored XSS, size limits

patterns.name: Sensitive route in JS: export/download
patterns.note: bulk-data endpoint: check authz on other users'/tenants' data and tamper with ids / date ranges

patterns.name: Sensitive route in JS: object by id
patterns.note: object-by-id route: swap the id for another user's (IDOR/BOLA), with and without your session

patterns.name: Sensitive route in JS: config/secrets
patterns.note: fetch it and look for keys, internal hosts or feature switches

patterns.name: Sensitive route in JS: GraphQL
patterns.note: try an introspection query, then field-level authz and query batching
